answer: An oasis farm buys lotus-water readings from agents. Pay once per registered sensor per hour, not per account: each reading carries a hardware signature and a sensor-hour identifier bound to its contracted payee that the payment ledger rejects if already spent. A mirror account can relay the reading but cannot claim a second reward. An independent installer must certify each new physical sensor, making extra paid identities require extra equipment and inspection. This limits duplicate payouts, not all fraud: stolen device keys or a dishonest installer can defeat the safeguard.
